1 فَغَمَهُ الطِيبُ , (S, K,) aor.
فَغَمَ , inf. n. فَغْمٌ and فُغُومٌ, (K,) The perfume stopped the air-passages of his nose. (S, K.) ―
-b2- And فَغَمَتِ الرَّائِحَةُ السُّدَّةَ The odour opened the obstruction of the nose: thus the verb has two contr. significations. (K.) ―
-b3- See also a trad. cited in art. فعم, conj. 4. ＝
-A2- فَغَمَ said of a rose, or flower, (S, TA,) aor.
فَغَمَ , inf. n. فُغُومٌ, (TA,) It opened; as also ↓ تفغّم . (S, TA.) ＝
-A3- فَغَمَ, (S, K, TA,) inf. n. فَغْمٌ; (TA;) and ↓ فاغم , (S, * K, TA,) inf. n. فِغَامٌ (S, TA) and مُفَاغَمَةٌ; (S;) He kissed (S, K, TA) him, or it, (S,) or a woman. (K, TA.) ―
-b2- And فَغَمَ said of a kid, (K, TA,) inf. n. فَغْمٌ, (TA,) He sucked (K, TA) the dug of his mother. (TA.) ＝
-A4- فَغِمَ بِهِ, (S, K,) aor.
فَغَمَ , (K,) inf. n. فَغَمٌ, (S,) He was, or became, attached to it, fond of it, or eagerly desirous of it. (S, K.) And فَغَمٌ الكَلْبِ signifies The dog's being attached, or accustomed, or habituated, to the chase. (TA.) ―
-b2- And فَغِمَ بِالمَكَانِ, (K, TA,) inf. n. فَغَمٌ, (TA,) He resided, stayed, dwelt, or abode, in the place; and kept, or clave, to it; (K, TA;) not quitting it. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
